paragraphs.title: The Purifying Spring and the Disappearance of Impurity

easy.explanation: The verse says, "there shall be a fountain opened."
easy.q: What shall be opened in that day?

answers: To the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
To the kings of the earth only
easy.explanation: The fountain is opened "to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem."
easy.q: To whom shall the fountain be opened?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, "I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land."
easy.q: What will be cut off from the land?

medium.explanation: The fountain is opened "for sin and for uncleanness."
medium.q: What is the purpose of the fountain?

medium.explanation: The fountain is connected with cleansing from uncleanness, or impurity.
medium.q: What does the word "uncleanness" describe in this passage?

answers: They shall no more be remembered
They shall be carried to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The verse says, "they shall no more be remembered."
medium.q: What will happen to the names of the idols?

answers: A fountain is opened, and the unclean spirit passes out
The sword awakes, and the sheep scatter
The third part remains, and silver is refined
challenge.explanation: The fountain represents cleansing, while the unclean spirit is removed from the land.
challenge.q: Which pair best describes both cleansing and the removal of impurity?

answers: It is undergoing a complete spiritual cleansing
It is becoming a place for false prophecy
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the removal of several sources of spiritual corruption.
challenge.q: What does the removal of idols, prophets, and the unclean spirit suggest about the land?

answers: Their names will be cut off and no longer remembered
Their names will be remembered more often
Their names will be preserved by the prophets
challenge.explanation: Both their removal and the end of their remembrance are stated.
challenge.q: What change is described concerning the idols?

paragraphs.title: The End of Prophecy and the Denial of Prophets

answers: Speaking lies in the name of the LORD
easy.explanation: His parents will say, "thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD."
easy.q: What will a person be accused of when he prophesies?

easy.explanation: The verse says that his father and mother shall thrust him through.
easy.q: Who will thrust through the person who prophesies?

easy.explanation: One will say, "I am no prophet; I am an husbandman."
easy.q: What will the prophets say about themselves?

answers: Because their prophecy will be rejected and regarded as deceitful
Because they will be chosen as rulers
medium.explanation: The passage says the prophets will be ashamed when they have prophesied.
medium.q: Why will the prophets be ashamed of their visions?

answers: A garment made of coarse material or hair
medium.explanation: The prophets will no longer wear a rough garment to deceive.
medium.q: What is a "rough garment" in this context?

answers: To present himself as an ordinary worker rather than a prophet
To announce that he is a leader
To ask for the fountain of cleansing
medium.explanation: The speaker denies being a prophet and claims to be a husbandman.
medium.q: What is the purpose of saying, "I am an husbandman"?

answers: They are regarded as liars, become ashamed, and deny their identity
They are honored, boastful, and made rulers
They are cleansed, chosen, and made shepherds
challenge.explanation: These three responses appear throughout verses 3–6.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the treatment of the prophets?

answers: They are trying to remove every outward sign of being prophets
They want to appear as kings
challenge.explanation: They will not wear the rough garment because they want to deceive or conceal their identity.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the prophets hiding their rough garments?

answers: The source of the marks on the man's body
challenge.explanation: The question specifically concerns the wounds in his hands.
challenge.q: What is being investigated by the question, "What are these wounds in thine hands?"

paragraphs.title: The Sword Against the Shepherd and the Leadership

answers: Against the shepherd and the man who is the LORD's fellow
Against the house of David only
easy.explanation: The verse says, "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow."
easy.q: Against whom is the sword commanded to awake?

answers: They shall be hidden in the fountain
easy.explanation: The verse says, "smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered."
easy.q: What will happen to the sheep when the shepherd is smitten?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, "I will turn mine hand upon the little ones."
easy.q: Upon whom will the LORD turn his hand?

medium.explanation: The scattering of the sheep shows the shepherd's leadership over them.
medium.q: What does the shepherd represent in the passage?

medium.explanation: The verse directly connects the shepherd's being smitten with the sheep being scattered.
medium.q: What is the result of smiting the shepherd?

answers: The lesser or more vulnerable people
medium.explanation: The expression refers to those under the shepherd's leadership, especially the lesser ones.
medium.q: In this passage, what are "the little ones"?

answers: When the shepherd is struck, the sheep scatter
When the sheep are struck, the shepherd becomes stronger
When the shepherd disappears, the fountain is purified
challenge.explanation: The sheep's scattering shows their dependence on the shepherd.
challenge.q: What relationship between leadership and the people is shown in the verse?

answers: The judgment affects the leader and another prominent figure associated with him
The judgment affects only the sheep
The judgment affects only false prophets
challenge.explanation: The verse names both the shepherd and the man who is his fellow.
challenge.q: What is suggested by mentioning both the shepherd and the man who is his fellow?

answers: The existing leadership is disrupted and the people are dispersed
The people unite around the shepherd
The prophets return to lead the people
challenge.explanation: The loss of the shepherd results in the scattering of the flock.
challenge.q: What change in the social order is suggested by the shepherd's being smitten and the sheep scattering?

paragraphs.title: The Survival and Refinement of the Third

easy.explanation: The verse says, "two parts therein shall be cut off and die."
easy.q: How many parts of the land shall be cut off and die?

easy.explanation: The passage says, "the third shall be left therein."
easy.q: How much shall be left in the land?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, "I will bring the third part through the fire."
easy.q: Through what will the third part be brought?

answers: To refining silver and trying gold
medium.explanation: The third part will be refined as silver and tried as gold.
medium.q: To what is the testing by fire compared?

medium.explanation: The verse says, "they shall call on my name."
medium.q: What will the third part do after being refined?

medium.explanation: The LORD says, "I will hear them."
medium.q: What will the LORD do when the third part calls?

answers: The third part survives but must undergo testing and purification
The third part survives without any change
The third part survives to conceal impurity
challenge.explanation: Survival is followed by refining and testing through fire.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the survival of the third part and the fire?

answers: The people call on the LORD, and He acknowledges them as His people
The people hide the LORD, and He scatters them
The people deny the LORD, and He remains silent
challenge.explanation: The LORD says, "It is my people," and they answer, "The LORD is my God."
challenge.q: What mutual relationship is described at the end of the passage?

answers: The survivors move from preservation to a renewed identity as God's people
The survivors disappear from the land
challenge.explanation: After being refined, the surviving group is recognized as the LORD's people.
challenge.q: What does the change from "the third" to "It is my people" suggest?
